articles.title: Stop counting tokens, start counting what ships
articles.excerpt: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50…
articles.body: When a developer gives an AI agent a coding task, the agent does more than answer once. It plans, generates code, runs tests, and repeats the process to correct errors. A single task can use 10 to 50 times more tokens than a basic chat prompt. The more useful the agent becomes, the more calls it makes. With per-token pricing, the workflows creating the most value can also become the most expensive. The financial pressure is already visible. Uber reportedly exhausted its entire 2026 AI budget by April after expanding its use of Claude Code. GitHub Copilot moved from flat-rate pricing to metered credits. Gartner predicts that AI coding token costs will surpass average developer salaries by 2028.
articles.author: Affan Syed

articles.title: The Download: the agentic web arrives and the drive for safer roads
articles.excerpt: This is today’s edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The agentic web is here In 2001, a decade after inventing the…
articles.body: This is today’s edition of The Download , our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what’s going on in the world of technology. The agentic web is here In 2001, a decade after inventing the World Wide Web, Tim Berners-Lee articulated a new vision: an internet navigated by autonomous software agents that address our every need, without requiring us to muck about with browsers and search engines ourselves. At the time, the idea seemed far-fetched. But a quarter-century on, AI agents are beginning to make it a reality. They can triage your inbox, do your grocery shopping, and even access your bank accounts. This new era is being called the agentic web. It will inevitably transform the internet—and whether the human web survives this transition is anyone’s guess.

articles.title: Deduplicate Your RAG Corpus Without Losing Its Citations
articles.excerpt: Your embedding deduplication can work perfectly while your citation index quietly forgets a source. If your ingestion loop keeps a single page row per contentHash, repeated content can replace an earl…
articles.body: Your embedding deduplication can work perfectly while your citation index quietly forgets a source. If your ingestion loop keeps a single page row per contentHash , repeated content can replace an earlier source relationship. The vector index looks tidy. The bibliography has selective memory. Lab note 042: our hypothesis is that embedding content and citation provenance need separate identities. The catch: contentHash has no specified hashing scope, so it can't safely stand for the exact text sent to your embedding model. Which URL should own a citation? Deduplicating embedding text must not delete the source observations that support its citations.

articles.body: Overview I’m Kaleb, a web developer based in Pompano Beach, Florida. articles.title: ESP32 vs ESP8266: diferencias reales y cuál elegir en 2026

articles.body: Publicado originalmente en iot.gripe . El ESP8266 fue el chip que hizo popular el IoT casero: por primera vez, un microcontrolador con Wi-Fi costaba lo mismo que un café. Su sucesor, el ESP32, llegó con mucho más de todo. Años después, en las tiendas siguen conviviendo los dos, a precios parecidos, y la pregunta se repite: ¿cuál compro? El ESP8266 fue durante años la placa Wi-Fi barata por excelencia, y todavía aparece en muchos tutoriales. Para proyectos nuevos, el ESP32 lo ha reemplazado casi por completo. En esta comparativa te cuento las diferencias que importan en la práctica y en qué casos el ESP8266 todavía tiene sentido. Para comparar todos los modelos de ESP32 entre sí, tienes la guía completa del ESP32. La respuesta corta Para un proyecto nuevo, elige un ESP32.

articles.title: API traffic monitoring: what to track, and how to set it up for a Node API
articles.excerpt: A customer emails: "your API has been timing out for an hour." Your uptime check is green, the error tracker is quiet and CPU looks fine. Somewhere in the last hour of traffic is the answer, and nothi…
articles.body: A customer emails: "your API has been timing out for an hour." Your uptime check is green, the error tracker is quiet and CPU looks fine. Somewhere in the last hour of traffic is the answer, and nothing you run kept it. API traffic monitoring closes that gap: record every request your API serves (who called which endpoint, with what payload, how long it took and what came back) and watch that traffic for errors, slow endpoints, breaking changes and abuse. This guide covers what to track, how to capture it in a Node API with working code, and the queries that turn raw traffic into answers. What is API traffic monitoring? API traffic monitoring is recording the requests an API serves and watching that traffic for change.

articles.body: SpaceX is building and operating two satellite networks at the moment, Starlink and Starshield. What’s the difference between the two, and who uses them? For more than a week in October 2026, Ukrainian drone operators found their high-speed satellite links shut off. Officials in Kyiv said that terminals for SpaceX ’s Starshield network stopped working at speeds of above 160 kilometers per hour (100 miles per hour) from Oct. 14, hampering efforts to conduct defensive operations and intercept Russian drones. Full connectivity was restored on Oct. 24, according to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy. The arguments over who did what continue, but the affair highlighted how little is publicly understood about Starshield — what it is, how it relates to Starlink , and how it is operated.

articles.title: 'Metroid Prime' needs some 'Resident Evil'-style remakes to rediscover its sci-fi shooter mojo
articles.excerpt: Nintendo's sci-fi shooter franchise is in dire straits, but we've got the solution to Samus's problems.
articles.body: Metroid Prime 4: Beyond was, unfortunately, not the return many were hoping for when it finally arrived on Nintendo Switch consoles in 2025. After five years in development at Retro Studios, the original makers of the Metroid Prime series, fans were greeted with annoying side characters, a bike for Samus to roam the barren landscape on, and a deeply unsatisfying ending. It’s a shame, considering how beloved the Metroid Prime series has been since the first title’s 2002 debut for the Nintendo GameCube. Many franchises were jumping from 2D to 3D at the turn of the millennium, and there were plenty of failures — but Metroid wasn’t one of them.

articles.title: Anthropic VS code extension on Cursor backdoored for nearly 12 hours
articles.excerpt: It's still unknown how attackers got access to Anthropic's verified Cursor account.
articles.body: An official extension for Anthropic’s Claude model was backdoored and threatened as many as 5,000 developers' machines, multiple sources reported Friday. Anthropic so far has yet to warn customers of the incident. The compromised package was a VS Code extension available in the marketplace of Cursor, a maker of AI-assisted developer tools, the company said Friday. The malicious version, 2.1.313, subsequently affected “at most 5,000 users,” presumably when they either downloaded it or their systems automatically fetched and installed it. Anthropic pushed version 2.1.314 several hours after the previous version became available on Cursor, according to independent researcher Kevin Beaumont.
